title: Debugging with Git
description: Combine git bisect, blame, log, and stash to debug regressions and investigate issues efficiently.

data.text: Git provides a complete debugging toolkit. Beyond bisect and blame, you can use stash to preserve work during investigation, revert to test fixes against old code, and use diff to compare behavior across commits. Combining these tools creates a systematic approach to regression investigation.

data.title: Systematic Git debugging
items: **1. Reproduce**: Verify the bug exists on the current branch
**2. Scope**: Identify which files and areas are affected
**3. Bisect**: Use git bisect to find the introducing commit
**4. Blame**: Use git blame to see who changed the relevant lines
**5. Fix**: Create a fix commit and validate
**6. Document**: Add a regression test to prevent recurrence

data.title: Full debugging session
data.code:
# Step 1: Reproduce the bug
git switch main
git pull origin main
npm start
# Confirm: bug is present

# Step 2: Find the introducing commit with bisect
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
# Find a tag where the bug was NOT present
git bisect good v2.1.0

# Step 3: Bisect runs automatically with a test
git bisect run npm test -- --grep "Regression"

# Step 4: Identify the commit and inspect
git show <bad-commit-sha>

# Step 5: Check blame for context
git blame src/auth/TokenService.cs

# Step 6: Create a fix and add a test
git switch -c fix/token-validation
# Fix the code
npm test -- --grep "Regression"  # Verify fix

git add src/auth/TokenService.cs
git commit -m "fix(auth): handle expired token gracefully"
git push origin fix/token-validation

data.text: If you have uncommitted work when you discover a bug, stash it before starting bisect. Bisect changes the working directory, so uncommitted changes will conflict or be lost.

data.title: Stash before bisect
data.code:
# Save uncommitted work
git stash push -m "WIP: debugging auth bug"

# Start bisect
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v2.1.0
# ... investigate ...

# Restore your work
git bisect reset
git stash pop

data.text: Use git diff to compare the behavior of a specific file or function between two commits. This helps identify exactly what changed when the regression was introduced.

data.title: Diff between the bad commit and its parent
data.code:
# See what changed in the bad commit
git diff <bad-sha>^! -- src/auth/TokenService.cs

# Compare behavior between two tags
git diff v2.1.0..v2.2.0 -- src/auth/

# See only function-level changes
git diff v2.1.0..v2.2.0 -- src/auth/TokenService.cs | grep -E '^[+-].*function'

data.text: Sometimes the fastest way to confirm a bug is caused by a specific commit is to revert it and see if the bug disappears. git revert creates a new commit that undoes the changes without rewriting history.

data.title: Revert a commit to confirm the cause
data.code:
# Revert the suspected commit
git revert --no-commit <bad-sha>

# Test: does the bug disappear?
npm test -- --grep "Regression"

# If confirmed, complete the revert
git revert --continue

# If not, abort
git revert --abort

data.title: Document regressions with tests
data.text: Every debugging session should end with a regression test. If a bug reached production, your test suite failed to catch it. Add a test that reproduces the bug and fails before the fix is applied.

items.question: Can I debug with Git on a Windows machine?
items.answer: Yes. All Git commands are cross-platform. Use PowerShell or Git Bash for the best experience.

items.question: What if bisect takes too long because tests are slow?
items.answer: Write a targeted reproduction test that runs in seconds. Use git bisect run with this fast test instead of the full suite.

items.question: Can I bisect across merge commits?
items.answer: Yes. Use git bisect skip for merge commits that are difficult to test. Bisect will skip them and continue searching.

items.question: How do I prevent the same regression from recurring?
items.answer: Add a regression test that reproduces the bug and fails before the fix. This test runs in CI on every future commit.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Follow a systematic workflow: reproduce → bisect → blame → fix → test
Stash uncommitted work before starting bisect
Use git diff to compare behavior between the bad commit and its parent
Revert to confirm the cause before applying a permanent fix
Always add a regression test after fixing a bug
